The facilities are excellent, but I think the cost is high.

I had my dog's ears cleaned and nails trimmed, but it was done in a separate room, so I couldn't see what was happening, which made me uneasy.

My dog ​​is very wary and doesn't like hospitals, but the staff seemed inexperienced and were clumsy, which traumatized him.

I've been using this hospital for over two years. They provide accurate, easy-to-understand explanations without causing anxiety, and they avoid excessive testing that would only burden the dog. They perform any necessary tests after the explanation. I appreciate their unobtrusive consideration of pet owners' anxieties.

I love small dogs, so I've been to several veterinary clinics over the past 20 years. I've mainly been to clinics in Minato, Setagaya, and Meguro, as well as Minato Yokohama Animal Hospital, which is renowned for its orthopedics.

I didn't want to write a review that was too easy, so I'll share my honest opinion after more than two years of use. Unfortunately, Setagaya in particular is seeing an increasing number of veterinary clinics that create anxiety, are businesslike, and only have stylish buildings, with unnecessarily large staff. Despite paying a considerable monthly fee, I rate this hospital as the best in Setagaya. I enjoy living with my dog ​​in his natural state. In terms of an important point, I think this hospital is one that gains insight and understanding into the relationship between owners and their dogs, as well as how the owners raise their dogs, with each visit.

We have been receiving care from them ever since they first opened. They carefully examine even the smallest concerns, such as when a pet accidentally swallows a flower stem or when a lump appears. The explanations of health checkup results are very detailed, and the nurses' love for animals is palpable, so I can leave them in their care with peace of mind.

My regular doctor was closed, so I had to take him in for an emergency appointment. My dog ​​had swallowed some grass from the roadside and injured his throat, causing him to choke and vomit even when drinking water. However, the vet simplified my explanation to simply saying he was "vomiting," so he took some blood and an abdominal X-ray, diagnosed him with "mild dehydration," and prescribed an IV drip and anti-nausea medication.

I asked again if the injury to his throat might be the cause, but he replied, "If he's vomiting, he might have diarrhea, so I'll also prescribe an intestinal regulator," and prescribed an additional intestinal regulator that was inappropriate for his condition.

I had no choice but to accept that they wouldn't listen to me there.

In the end, my dog ​​continued coughing that night, so I took him to my regular doctor the next morning. The doctor identified the pain by palpation of his throat, and he quickly recovered with an IV drip of antibiotics and anti-inflammatory painkillers.

From this experience, I became concerned that the veterinarian's assumptions and preconceptions may not fully reflect the owner's specific explanation in the diagnosis, so I would like to share my thoughts here. 

I hope this will help you choose a veterinary hospital.

I contacted my nearest animal hospital, but I felt uneasy about their phone service, so I researched and contacted this hospital instead. They listened carefully to my situation, so I decided to go with them. Everyone was kind, and I felt confident entrusting my pet to them, so I will definitely come back here next time.

Thank you very much.
The veterinarian and staff are all very kind.

The veterinarians and nurses are all very kind. I've been to many animal hospitals, but this one is the kindest, and I felt completely at ease leaving my pet here. The prices are also reasonable, and it's a hospital I want to keep going to.

My beloved family member was injured due to a misdiagnosis, and then sent home after being told there was no fracture when in fact there was. Their attitude and handling of the situation were appalling. I hope this information will be helpful to others.
